interruption.whatThisRunProduced: Real model calls across the hold-out corpus, no completed evaluation, no publication. It got substantially further than 145a2afba7b8 — that one died on the fixture coupling at the first model record; this one exercised the model through several records before one answer came back unparseable.
interruption.theFindingThisExposes: The lane cannot record the very signal its own design says it is measuring. investigation-roles.ts states, deliberately, 'One completion per role execution. No repair round, no retry: a role that could re-ask on a refused answer would hide the model-quality signal the lane is measuring.' A refused answer IS therefore a measurement. But the refusal propagates as an exception and aborts the whole experiment, so the measurement is destroyed along with the other twenty-nine records. benchmark-evaluation.ts contains no try/catch at all: there is no per-record error path, and BenchmarkOutcome requires an actualStopKind from the InvestigationStop enum, in which 'the role returned an answer the domain refuses' is not representable.
interruption.whyThisIsNotFixedInThisRun: Adding a per-record error path changes what a benchmark result can BE. That is a public type, and its consumers include the regression gate and the LangSmith projection. Under .claude/rules/autonomy.md that is the 'surprise scope' stop rule: a Tier-2 area this item did not plan to touch. It is recorded as a FAIL row on AIC-19 rather than absorbed quietly, which is what the gate exists to do.
interruption.whyThisIsNotVoided: The model executed against hold-out scenarios. As with 145a2afba7b8, calling that 'produced no information' would be false.
